SUPERSEDES (within hours, same thread): the just-recorded reflection-layer insight describing the grok-text-relay-v1 diff as uncommitted/awaiting-review is now stale at the surface. The diff was committed by Anthony (with Claude Sonnet 4.6 co-author attribution) on another seat WHILE this HQ instance was writing the chronicle records. Commit hash dc63f86, message 'feat(bridge): text-relay path + dispatch helper + submit-text CLI command', timestamp Mon May 11 08:24:29 -0400, all 6 files included matching the locked scope (337 lines in text_relay.py, 36 in dispatch.py, +102 in cli.py, +4 in __init__.py, +7 in pending_writes.py, +9/-14 in mcp_filtered.py). Branch main is now in sync with origin/main — push happened too.

ACTUAL STATE for next instance arrival:
- Working tree clean.
- Branch main = origin/main.
- All 6 files of the relay implementation live in HEAD (dc63f86).
- The prior reflection insight's design-call documentation, test results, and replay command are STILL correct and useful — only the 'uncommitted' framing is wrong.

PICKUP at next arrival: the optional follow-ups remain open. (1) tests/clients/test_text_relay.py reproducing the 5 scenarios + structural equivalence guard. (2) README update covering the submit-text subcommand. (3) approve/commit mutation paths for relay_attribution.approved_by and .committed_by (only if Anthony wants the 4-actor chain self-contained on the proposal file; current design leaves those None and relies on reviewed_by + audit log).

METHODOLOGY NOTE (self-model relevance): the prior insight + handoff stated 'working tree dirty' based on a git status check from about 6 minutes earlier. The state shifted while the chronicle writes were in flight. Same-machine cross-seat concurrency can race the chronicle writer — verification has a freshness half-life. Next time: verify state immediately before writing a snapshot-style handoff, not several actions earlier. Single re-check at the end of close_session preparation would have caught this.
